correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructed Gaussian conditional-variance minimization. For nonnegative regression weights the exact Hessian is positive and a strict sum/difference identity reduces all site designs to one symmetric scalar minimizer. For a negative regression weight strict concavity in its site forces a collided site or endpoint, and the endpoint Schur complement yields eta(1-rho^2). Monotonic comparison proves unique critical rho; the companion verifier reproduced all critical symbolic identities and rational Gaussian-matrix certificates; finite probes are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Direct finite-noise phase classification is not a relabeling of independent-noise optimal placements or an immediate consequence of known high-noise asymptotics. Source claims and implications were compared: only the rho=0 slice and eta-to-infinity behavior are established by closest prior results. The all-parameter global two-geometry theorem, exact critical positive eta and discontinuous optimizer switch require the new coefficient-sign convexity/concavity classification. Historical priority remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: Historical results may give this special case through a different correlated-error experimental-design parametrization.

value.rationale: The theorem sharply decides a practical nonlinear sensing choice: for positively correlated measurement errors, when does a deliberately uninformative endpoint observation outperform two informative interior observations? It gives an exact finite-noise phase diagram, critical variance and discontinuous global placement change. The object is a natural Brownian-bridge integral and the precise risk is the canonical optimal Gaussian posterior variance. Not a mere specialization of rate bounds or an isolated cheap example.
